raw.query: SELECT c.lead_s, SUM(c.numerator_worker_seconds) / SUM(c.denominator_worker_seconds) AS aggregate_cost_ratio FROM provenance.v_dim d JOIN provenance.v_cost_ratio c ON c.run_id = d.run_id WHERE d.is_current = TRUE AND c.is_current = TRUE AND d.experiment = 'a2x' AND c.experiment = 'a2x' AND c.policy = 'forecast' AND c.lead_s IN (15, 30, 45, 165) AND c.denominator_kind = 'deployable_static_c8' AND c.denominator_window_mismatch = FALSE GROUP BY c.lead_s ORDER BY c.lead_s;
raw.observed: Aggregate cost ratio declines from 2.3000537850024174 at 15 s to 2.1617232564851223 at 165 s; across 11 paired windows, cost ratio systematically decreases with a mean relative drop of 7.72% (min: 2.91% in e7, max: 18.36% in e16).
raw.claimed: Actuated on forecast issue time, the cost is essentially lead-invariant across the archive's realizable 15-165 s issued-lead range.
raw.evidence: Every single one of the 11 paired windows demonstrates a cost reduction as lead time increases, contradicting the assertion of lead invariance.
raw.fix: Soften the wording from 'essentially lead-invariant' to 'exhibiting a mild, systematic lead-dependent drop in cost (averaging ~7.7% from L=15 to 165 s)'.
